pages.summary: Measured data for system identification, and input signals to measure with.
body: `iddata` holds an output y and an input u (a column each, or several), sampled every Ts seconds, with names and units: `data.y` and `data.u` are the signals, `data(k)` picks samples, and `detrend`, `size` and `plot` take it. A time series has no input (`[]`). `idinput` makes an input for an experiment: random Gaussian (`'rgs'`), random binary (`'rbs'`), pseudorandom binary of maximum length (`'prbs'`) or a sum of sines (`'sine'`), within a band of frequencies (fractions of the Nyquist frequency) and between two levels. A binary input excites the system as strongly as its limits allow.
syntax: Output and input, sampled every Ts.
data = iddata(y, u, Ts, 'OutputName', name, 'InputName', name)
An input signal of N samples.

pages.summary: Linear models by least squares: ARX models with an input, AR models of time series.
body: An ARX model is A(q) y(t) = B(q) u(t - nk) + e(t): na past outputs and nb past inputs, nk samples of delay, the coefficients found by least squares. It is also a discrete transfer function B/A, so that `step`, `bode`, `lsim` and the rest take it. `ar` fits A(q) y(t) = e(t) to a time series, by least squares or (`'yw'`) the Yule-Walker equations.
syntax: An AR model of order n.

pages.summary: Polynomial models with their own noise: ARMAX, output-error and Box-Jenkins.
body: These fit by prediction error minimization, each with a noise model of its own. ARMAX: A(q) y(t) = B(q) u(t - nk) + C(q) e(t), the noise filtered through C/A; output error: y(t) = B(q)/F(q) u(t - nk) + e(t), white noise on the output, the model fitted to the simulated output; Box-Jenkins: y(t) = B(q)/F(q) u(t - nk) + C(q)/D(q) e(t), the system and the noise each with its own poles.
syntax: An ARMA model of a time series.
sys = bj(data, [nb nc nd nf nk])

examples.title: White noise on the output
examples.intro: The noise here is added to the output, so an output-error model has the right structure; ARX, which assumes noise filtered through 1/A, is pulled away from the system.

pages.summary: State-space models found from data: by subspace identification, and refined by prediction errors.
body: `n4sid` finds a model of nx states in innovations form, x(t+1) = A x(t) + B u(t) + K e(t), y(t) = C x(t) + D u(t) + e(t), from the data's projections, without iterations (D is 0 unless `'Feedthrough'` is true). `ssest` starts there and refines the model by prediction error minimization, in observer canonical form. The states are a basis of the model's own choosing; the poles, the frequency response and the outputs do not depend on it.

examples.title: A resonance found again
examples.intro: The data come from a system with poles at 0.9 e^(±0.3i).

body: np poles and nz zeros (np - 1 unless given), the input held between samples as sampled data are taken; the result is a continuous `tf`, for `step`, `bode` and the rest.

pages.summary: Models' outputs set against measured data, and a model's simulated response.
body: `compare` simulates each model with the data's input (or predicts K steps ahead) and draws its output over the measured one, the legend naming each model after its variable with the fit 100 (1 - |y - ŷ| / |y - mean(y)|) per cent: 100 is a perfect match, 0 no better than the mean. The initial state is estimated for simulations. `sim` gives a model's output for an input or a data set's input.

examples.title: Two orders judged on fresh data

pages.summary: Prediction errors of a model, and the analysis of its residuals.
body: `pe` gives the one-step (or K-step) prediction errors on a data set, as a data set (`e.y` the errors). `resid` draws the residuals' autocorrelation and their cross-correlation with the input, with 99% bounds: for a good model both stay within them, the residuals being white and owing nothing to the input. Its outputs give the residuals and the correlations.

pages.summary: A polynomial model's polynomials with their uncertainties, and a model shown with them.
body: `polydata` gives A, B, C, D and F (those the model does not have are 1, or 0 for B without an input), and the standard deviations of their coefficients. `present` shows the model with each coefficient's standard deviation.
syntax: [A, B, C, D, F, dA, dB, dC, dD, dF] = polydata(sys)

pages.summary: Information criteria and final prediction errors, to choose among models.
body: `aic` gives the Akaike information criterion, N log(V) + 2 n (plus terms that do not change between models of the same data), where V is the loss and n the number of parameters: smaller is better, the second term charging for each parameter. `'AICc'` corrects it for few samples, `'nAIC'` normalizes it, and `'BIC'` charges log(N) a parameter instead. `fpe` gives Akaike's final prediction error, V (1 + n/N)/(1 - n/N).
